notes:
I couldn't write the Job 40 notes. My only way to read the approved sites stopped working before I could open a single page.

The first batch of fetches was meant to pull Enduring Word, the BibleHub commentaries (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Wesley) and the NET Bible notes. It ended with "no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn", nothing came back, and every later call was refused the same way. My other tools have no internet access, so I couldn't reach any of the listed sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read no sources, I have nothing I can back with a URL, and I haven't written any notes from memory.

**Next steps:** in a new turn, when the search tool is available again, I'll go through these in order:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:**
  - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-40/
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/job/40.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/job/40.htm
  - biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/job/40.htm
  - preceptaustin.org, for vv. 4–5 and 8 especially
- **Tradition differences:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu or biblehub.com/commentaries/wesley/job/40.htm), Spurgeon on vv. 4–5, plus Ligonier, Desiring God and 1517 on Job's repentance and v. 8.
- **Other views:**
  - netbible.org notes on "Behemoth" (v. 15), the words for lotus and reeds (vv. 21–22) and the Jordan (v. 23)
  - bibleodyssey.org on Behemoth and ancient Near Eastern myth
  - gotquestions.org on whether Behemoth was a dinosaur, a hippo or an elephant (a popular modern debate)
  - newadvent.org for the Church Fathers, such as Gregory the Great's reading of Behemoth as the devil, if the page has it

You can also paste the text of any of these pages here. I'll then write verse-by-verse notes from that text only, with a URL for each point.
